inputs.original_text: A baby stopped breathing in a crowded TSA line at JFK on Thursday, and an ICE agent stepped in while the family was in distress. That deserves recognition as a humane act—but the Department of Homeland Security releasing footage doesn’t turn one moment into proof that an entire enforcement system serves everyone fairly. We can appreciate an individual helping a family and still ask why public safety is so often framed as a defense of institutions rather than a commitment to protecting vulnerable people consistently.
inputs.modified_text: An ICE agent stepping in when a baby stopped breathing in a crowded TSA line at JFK on Thursday was the right, humane thing to do—and the family deserved that help. But the Department of Homeland Security shouldn’t get to turn one act of care into a defense of an enforcement system that doesn’t protect everyone equally. Real public safety means consistently protecting people in moments of vulnerability, not using a crisis as institutional good publicity.
